doc.title: Ingrid Sertso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014

title: Titles of poems and songs
summary: Titles sometimes come first; her poem Africa won an award.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Some things never change. Wow. Just to wrap up, I’ve really enjoyed this conversation. When you write a poem or a song, at what point do you think of the title? And are titles important?

Yes, sometimes the title is first. I wrote a song, “Africa.” It’s my only poem that actually won an award by the Washington Poet’s Gallery. They had asked me for a poem and I sent them “Africa.” And then some — no usually I have the plan, what I’m going to do, and that’s the title. Like “Four Seasons” — spring, summer, winter fall — that’s on my last CD, and so on and so on.
